heuristics.name: random-walk heuristic
heuristics.statement: On the N=(r+1)/2 classes the R-adding walk with look-ahead behaves, for collision purposes, like a random mapping up to a factor (1-1/R)^(-1/2) in expected collision time.
heuristics.support: Teske ANTS 1998; Brent-Pollard; Bernstein-Lange-Schwabe PKC 2011 for the negation-map variant.
heuristics.limitations: Not a theorem. A 1.4x degradation of the collision exponent still leaves success probability 0.398 >= 0.39.
heuristics.extrapolation: Applied from the literature and from the toy experiment to production P-256.

heuristics.name: fruitless-cycle bound
heuristics.statement: Fruitless cycles longer than 64 steps are negligible for R=2048.
heuristics.limitations: Depends on R and the look-ahead escape. Stated only for R=2048.
heuristics.extrapolation: Applied from that analysis to this parameter choice.

limitations: Analytic construction; no full-size execution or independent qualification.
Success uses standard Pollard-rho heuristics H1 and H2, disclosed in this file.
Instruction bounds are analytical upper bounds, not Callgrind measurements of a P-256 kernel.
This is a generic best-known-style accounting, not a novelty or practical-break claim.
